title_as_printed: Table 5 (no caption printed; text: experimentally determined temperature-pressure-molar volume combinations at the boundary surface between the heterogeneous and the homogeneous one-phase region, at constant composition ('isopleths'))
property_description: ternary fluid-phase boundary (isopleth) points by the synthetic method: for a mixture of fixed overall composition (mol% H2O, CH4, CaCl2), the (T, P) at which the heterogeneous two-fluid system becomes a homogeneous single phase on heating at constant volume (break point of the PT isochore, with visual and electrolytic-resistance indication), and the molar volume V of the homogeneous fluid at that point. The paper does not say which side of the boundary (bubble or dew, water-rich or methane-rich) each point is, and the points are close to the critical region; the overall composition is therefore NOT a coexisting-phase composition except at the boundary of the bulk phase.
pressure_note: absolute pressure of the homogeneous fluid at the phase boundary (strain-gauge transducers calibrated against a dead-weight gauge; back-up fluid behind the piston); synthetic method, basis saturation (boundary point)

value.what: molar volume of the homogeneous ternary fluid at the phase-boundary point, per mole of mixture (H2O + CH4 + salt as printed in mol%)

composition.other_species: composition of the whole ternary mixture in mol% (H2O + CH4 + CaCl2 = 100, salt counted as one formula unit), set per block from the label rows; text: 0.5, 1.6 and 6.0 weight percent of CaCl2 relative to water (0.065, 0.197 and 0.78 mol%), all at 23.5 mol% CH4

skip_rows.reason: isopleth label rows: composition printed beside the first three data rows, written as its own label row (v2.1 rule 10)

conversion_needs: mol% of the ternary mixture to salt molality: m_salt = x_salt / (x_H2O * 0.018015); CH4 content as overall mole fraction, or salt-free x_CH4 = CH4/(CH4+H2O)
the boundary point is a homogenisation (phase-disappearance) point: the overall composition equals the composition of the remaining phase, but the incipient phase composition is unknown
notes: Scanned page (1-bit CCITT image, OCR text layer); every number transcribed from the page image and diffed against the OCR text layer (corrections listed in paper.json). Temperatures are printed to 1 K. Each block is one isopleth; T is not monotonic along a block (it passes through a temperature minimum as P rises), as in the paper's Figs. 1-4. Text says the shift produced by CaCl2 appears to reflect incomplete ionic dissociation at high temperatures.
